question.text: A person standing at point <math><mi>P</mi></math> sees angle of elevation of the top of a building, whose base is <math><mn>50</mn></math> meters away, to be <math><msup><mrow><mn>60</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup></math>. Another building whose base is <math><mn>20</mn></math> meters away from the base of the first building and is between the observer and first building has height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> meters, then the maximum possible height (in meters) of this second building is (Take <math><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>1.73</mn></math>)

solution.text:
Since initial building can be observed from the point P
⇒h≤303=301.73=51.90 meters
